items.text: Codebase already has two production-tested in-memory TTL cache implementations in agent-manager: (1) pricing service cache (internal/pricing/service.go) uses sync.RWMutex + map with expiresAt per entry, manual invalidation on updates, and staleness metadata (FetchedAt, ExpiresAt, IsStale fields). (2) Stats orchestration cache (internal/orchestration/stats.go) uses 30s fixed TTL with sync.RWMutex. Both are custom-built using Go stdlib — no external cache libraries. Command-center should follow the same pattern with per-source TTLs and staleness metadata in API responses.

errgroup is the established concurrent fan-out pattern in the codebase (used in git-control-tower/repo_status_service.go for parallel git operations, scenario-stack-governor for parallel module checks). The agent-manager stats orchestration uses sync.WaitGroup for parallel DB queries. For HTTP fan-out to 3 sources, errgroup.WithContext is the better fit — it propagates context cancellation and collects the first error. Pattern: g, ctx := errgroup.WithContext(ctx); g.Go(func() error { ... }); if err := g.Wait(); err != nil { ... }.

The swarm-manager circuit breaker (internal/execution/circuit_breaker.go) is file-backed and per-item (tracks consecutive failures with threshold + cooldown). For command-center's per-source circuit breaker, a simpler in-memory model suffices: track consecutive failures per source, trip after N failures, half-open after cooldown period, reset on success. No file persistence needed since command-center restarts should reset breakers (sources may have recovered).

The command-center scenario does NOT exist yet — no files at scenarios/command-center/. The execute/command-center-scenario-scaffold backlog item (which command-center-api-aggregator depends on) must create the scenario before implementation begins. The API aggregator will be built inside scenarios/command-center/api/.

items.context: Command-center makes parallel requests to 3 sources (LPBS, Swarm Manager, Vrooli Core). If one source is slow or down, it shouldn't block the entire response. Need to decide how to handle per-source timeouts and partial response assembly.

options.label: Per-source context timeout (e.g., 5s per source) with errgroup — return partial results from fast sources if one times out, fill timed-out source from cache
options.rationale: Best UX — dashboards render quickly with whatever data is available. Cache serves stale data for timed-out sources. Each source gets its own context.WithTimeout child. Requires staleness metadata so UI knows which data is fresh vs stale.

options.label: Single request-level timeout (e.g., 10s) — all sources must respond or the whole request fails
options.rationale: Simpler to implement. But one slow source degrades all dashboards. Bad UX when only one source is having issues.

items.context: When serving cached data (especially stale-on-failure), the UI needs to know data freshness. Need to decide the staleness reporting format in command-center's API responses.

options.label: Per-source staleness object in every response: {"sources": {"lpbs": {"status": "fresh", "fetched_at": "...", "age_seconds": 12}, "swarm": {"status": "stale", "fetched_at": "...", "age_seconds": 45, "error": "timeout"}}}
options.rationale: UI can render freshness indicators per data section. Transparent about data quality. Consistent structure across all dashboard endpoints.

options.label: Single response-level freshness flag: {"data_fresh": true, "oldest_source_age_seconds": 45}
options.rationale: Simpler. UI shows one freshness badge. But loses granularity — can't distinguish which source is stale.

items.topic: Go package structure for the aggregator
items.context: Need to define how the command-center API code is organized. The execute spec mentions source clients, cache layer, dashboard composers, and gap registry.

options.label: Flat package main with service-per-file (matching LPBS pattern): main.go, server.go, routes.go, cache.go, client_lpbs.go, client_swarm.go, client_scenarios.go, dashboard_mission_control.go, dashboard_hive.go, etc., gaps.go
options.rationale: Consistent with LPBS pattern already in the codebase. Simple, no import cycles. Each dashboard handler composes from source clients. Good for a single-binary service.

options.label: Internal packages: internal/source/{lpbs,swarm,scenarios}, internal/cache, internal/dashboard, internal/gaps — with main.go wiring
options.rationale: Stronger encapsulation. Clear dependency boundaries. But more boilerplate for a relatively simple service. Matches agent-manager pattern.

plan_updates: Incorporated settled round 2 decisions (widen requireAdminOrService, per-dashboard endpoints, three separate LPBS endpoints). Added findings on existing cache and fan-out patterns from the codebase. New decisions focus on implementation-level details: timeout strategy, staleness metadata format, and package structure.
